condition.label: whiplash-associated disorder
condition.distinctions: Acute versus persistent WAD and grades I, II and III are attributes with different trial applicability; suspected fracture/instability is not routine exercise eligibility.

scope.population: Chronic WAD grades II and III; Ages 18–65, chronic WAD grades I/II, 3 months–5 years; excluded nerve-root compromise; Ages 18–65, chronic WAD
scope.stage: Varies by source; acute/recent versus chronic and symptom irritability are explicitly retained. Unknown stage remains unknown.
scope.operativeStatus: Nonsurgical evidence predominates; no postoperative protocol approved or inferred.
scope.exclusions: Source-specific exclusions are applicability boundaries, not diagnosis-wide contraindications. Coexisting conditions and independently selected joint limits retain precedence.
scope.uncertainty:
- Ordinary training: acute trauma/uncleared fracture or instability is not a generic workout state. Once assessed, recovery-stage and symptom-response modifications can allow activity; later strengthening cannot be scheduled solely from an app's elapsed time. WAD-G1 supports severe-pain avoidance in acute examples; chronic trial arms use different pain-response approaches.
- Supportive candidates: gentle cervical ROM, low-load cervical isometrics, neck endurance/control, staged scapular/general conditioning. Exact grade, stage, neurologic status and execution matter; never substitute neck bridges or externally loaded cervical exercises for gentle isometrics.
- No universal numeric ROM, external-load ceiling, recurrence threshold or automated dose established. Restriction-only draft while stage/clearance unknown; no fabricated “clinician approved” status.

sources.outcomes: Ludvigsson et al., 2015 RCT (online 2014). DOI 10.1097/AJP.0000000000000123, PMID 24918474, PMC4352069; FT via XML. 216 adults chronic WAD grades II/III. Twelve weeks neck-specific exercise (NSE), NSE plus behavioral approach, or prescribed general activity; two supervised visits/week plus home exercise. NSE progressed gentle isometrics to resistance/endurance, symptom/capacity tailored. NSE arms had greater disability improvement at 3/6 months; no significant difference between NSE arms. One arm avoided pain aggravation; behavioral arm deemphasized temporary increases. Adverse-event section not found. Thus no evidence for one universal zero-pain rule, mandatory grade-III exclusion, or unrestricted pain-pushing; clinician monitoring is material.

sources.outcomes: Michaleff et al., 2014 PROMISE RCT. DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(14)60457-8, full article PDF mirror. FT. 172 adults 18–65, WAD I/II, 3 months–5 years; comprehensive 20-session PT exercise versus one advice session/phone support. At 14 weeks pain difference 0.0/10 (95% CI −0.7 to 0.7); no advantage at 6/12 months. No serious adverse events recorded. Nerve-root compromise/grade III excluded, limiting scope; not proof grade III exercise is unsafe (WAD-P1 studied it). Contrary evidence prevents promising that more sessions or complexity necessarily improves outcomes.
sources.uncertainty: Primary pain difference zero at 14 weeks; intensive package not superior; grade III exclusion is applicability boundary
sources.harms: No serious adverse events. Adverse effects in five exercise and four advice patients: headache, musculoskeletal symptoms, symptom exacerbation or stiffness; no withdrawal for adverse effects. Open-ended questioning at three-month assessment.
sources.limitations: Primary pain difference zero at 14 weeks; intensive package not superior; grade III exclusion is applicability boundary Trial exclusions delimit studied applicability; they do not establish general contraindications.
